terms.definition: The bottom number in a fraction, counting the equal parts the whole is split into.
terms.function: In 3/4 the denominator 4 says the whole has 4 equal parts.
terms.whereItIs: The changing number plate below the active bar.
terms.whyItMatters: It sizes every piece of the fraction.

terms.definition: The amount each equal part represents.
terms.function: More parts mean each part is smaller — 1/8 is smaller than 1/2.
terms.whereItIs: The single filled segment in each bar.
terms.whyItMatters: Part size is the real meaning behind the denominator.

terms.definition: Segments of the whole that are all the same size.
terms.function: The denominator counts how many of these equal segments exist.
terms.whereItIs: The even segments cut into each bar.
terms.whyItMatters: Equal cutting is what makes denominators honest.

terms.definition: A shared denominator used to add, subtract, or compare fractions.
terms.function: 1/2 and 1/3 both become sixths (3/6 and 2/6) to be added.
terms.whereItIs: The matching part size needed across two bars.
terms.whyItMatters: Only same-sized parts can be counted together.
